mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays depressed while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, weekday trip chains stay home-centered and discretionary shopping rebounds only weakly. That pattern should keep RETAIL_REC below its prior 4-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying below -25 and RESIDENTIAL staying above +5 on weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week recovery in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS signals renewed out-of-home circulation and errand bundling. When both move up together, retail visits should improve within two weeks as shoppers add discretionary stops to essential trips.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both rise for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days after both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS post back-to-back weekly increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT indicates reduced access to dense commercial areas and suppresses incidental shopping. If transit remains weak, RETAIL_REC should stay lower over the next four weeks than in the prior four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points below its prior week and stays below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean while TRANSIT remains below -25 for at least two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS are positive and rising, outdoor leisure competes with indoor retail for discretionary time and spending. That substitution should hold retail-and-recreation below its recent average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days after PARKS crosses above zero and stays positive.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT implies more commuting-linked foot traffic and more opportunities for same-day shopping. That combined effect should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays at or below its prior 4-week mean even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT trend upward for four consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM declines while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, households are consolidating essential trips at home and avoiding discretionary add-on visits. Retail mobility should weaken within two weeks under that pattern.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -15 while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above +8
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -15 and RESIDENTIAL remains at or above +8.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in TRANSIT with WORKPLACES still suppressed implies mobility is reopening faster than office attendance, which channels trips into mixed-purpose commercial corridors. Retail should rise over the next month in that regime.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for two weeks while WORKPLACES remains below -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days after TRANSIT rises for two weeks and WORKPLACES stays below -30.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state week, a simultaneous rise in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL indicates substitution toward local, non-retail activity and less time spent in shopping districts. This should hold RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its prior 4-week mean even though PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both remain above their recent 4-week levels.
